fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review that builds the five-component framework Reflexive Prompt Engineering (Section 1.2). General_Guidance: 'prompts can be intentionally crafted or augmented with instructions to avoid bias' (3.1.3). ICL: balanced, randomly ordered few-shot examples, debiasing and counterfactual attribute flipping (3.1.1). Thought_Generation: chain-of-thought with ethical checkpoints (3.1.2). Self_Criticism: separate verification step 'Plan verification questions to fact-check this draft' (3.1.2). Object_of_Critique: chain-of-thought explanations as an 'illusion of transparency' (3.1.2). Learning_Content: the work positions responsible prompt engineering as a core competency of AI literacy and names its incorporation into curricula and training programmes (Abstract, Section 2.2, Section 4). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender and race appear only as attributes to flip and in a cited replacement example, not as an axis the work analyses. AN_Harm_Types None: stereotyping, toxicity and the Gemini misrepresentation incident are cited from other sources or named as tool targets, the framework establishes no harm mechanism of its own. Mitigation Proposed: debiasing through prompt design, documentation, stakeholder involvement and human oversight are recommended without an own or synthesised assessment. AN_Task None: recruitment, performance reviews and legal analysis illustrate a general framework. AN_Theory_Reference No: value-sensitive design is named as an aligned responsibility-by-design approach and frames neither gender nor bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment on Flan-PaLM 540B with a people-diversity dataset (105 professions) and a culture-diversity dataset, automated entropy and max-gap metrics and human side-by-side ratings. CCSV combines self-critique and revision (Self_Criticism) with sampling several drafts and self-voting (Ensembling); the baselines comprise 5-shot exemplars (ICL), zero- and few-shot chain-of-thought (Thought_Generation) and the 0-shot instruction 'Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity' (General_Guidance), which failed. Evaluated: CCSV outperforms all baselines on automated and human evaluation (Sections 5.1, 6). Fine-tuning with CCSV data is named only as future work and not coded as In_Training. Language_Culture through the culture-diversity task rated by humans (Section 6.2). Erasure: under-representation or erasure of demographic groups in the responses, measured as entropy close to 0. Exclusionary_Norms: the work's own baseline output defaults to 'only white male CEOs' when the prompt is under-specified, which the work attributes to implicit assumptions of the model (Abstract, Section 1). AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical with Implicit_Only: the analysis uses fixed knowledge-graph labels male, female and other, and the work itself states that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female and that the gender signal is incomplete (footnote 2, Limitations), so no gender beyond the binary is a category of the analysis; boundary case for the domain experts. Identity: corpus and text titles differ in wording, see identity_check. AN_Task None: general LLM evaluation without a professional task.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review of AI and machine learning in social work: predictive risk analytics in child welfare, mental-health chatbots, NLP for case notes, automated case management, AI in social work education. AN_Bias_Axes Race_Ethnicity: the review develops the over-representation of families from certain ethnic backgrounds in child-abuse risk prediction as its own worked example (4.1) and returns to the Allegheny case (4.1.1). Socioeconomic (housing vouchers, Turner et al. 2020, absent from the reference list) and Language_Culture (English-only chatbots) appear only as single-sentence cited cases in 4.1.1, and gender only in the enumeration 'racial, gender, or socio-economic disparities', so they stay uncoded. AN_Harm_Types Indirect_Discrimination: the review's own argument in 4.1 places the disadvantage in risk scores learned from historical data that affect access to services and child welfare interventions, an allocation through biased data rather than the attribute itself; the work does not classify the discrimination. Mitigation Proposed: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing); auditing, transparency, involvement of social workers and community members, AI training (Organisational_Process); none is assessed. AN_Task: predictive risk assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support), mental-health chatbots (Counselling_Client_Communication), NLP summaries of case notes and automated documentation (Documentation_Recording), AI tools and AI-driven personalised learning in social work education and training (Teaching_Further_Education, Sections 5.3.3 and 6.1.1). Source quality: several in-text citations do not match the reference list, for example 'Baker et al., 2021' cited for NLP documentation while reference [3] is a review of AI in net-zero building design, 'Chukwunweike et al.' cited for predictive analytics in social work while reference [9] concerns loop execution in deep-learning systems, and 'Turner et al., 2020' absent from the list; this limits the evidential weight of the cited case studies without changing the publication type.

fields.AN_Notes: Reflective empirical account of the co-creation workshops of the Horizon Europe MAMMOth project with marginalised groups (women at risk of social exclusion, young people, ethnic minorities, migrants, LGBTQI+ early career researchers), each opened by a training module on AI bias, feeding user and research requirements of an AI bias toolkit. Mitigation Demonstrated: the training within co-creation was applied and is reported only through facilitator and participant reflections, without a completed assessment of an effect on AI bias, although the work calls its approach an evaluation. AN_Task Other_Task: AI-based home loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search as use cases, outside social work. AN_Bias_Axes: Gender through the training examples added by DAF (generative AI answers on fathers and mothers, gendered job endings in Google Translate, Section 5.1); Religion and Physical_Appearance through the ranked facial attributes for identity verification (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos, Section 4.1). Race_Ethnicity stays uncoded: postal codes as proxy of race appear only as a parenthetical example of a toolkit challenge (Section 4) and the participant consensus that white males benefit most from credit scoring is a single reported perception (Section 4.2); the enumeration 'gender, age, ethnic origin, and sexual orientation' and the participant groups are not coded either. AN_Harm_Types: Stereotyping from the gender-role examples demonstrated in the training, Indirect_Discrimination from the proxy bias the project's own toolkit is built to address. Gender is treated through examples only, without a stated or recognisable understanding, hence Absent and Unclear. AN_Theory_Reference Yes: critical and social-justice perspectives on participatory design (power relations, 'box-ticking', ethics-washing) frame the treatment of AI bias and training; boundary between framing tradition and methodological label. Soziale_Arbeit teilweise: participants include recipients of social protection services and domestic violence victims recruited via civil society organisations, but no social work practice is addressed. The Markdown conversion duplicates and scrambles parts of Sections 4.3 to 5.3; all quotes come from coherent passages.
